_note: A two-person conversation. `who` picks the voice. `text` is what the line says (shown nowhere: the video has no captions). `say`, when given, is how the voice reads it. `pause` is extra frames of silence after a line.

opener.text: QR codes are everywhere now. Slides, tickets, posters. Your screen.

talk.text: The speaker's slides are a QR code. And my phone is dead.
You don't need it. Win, Shift, Q.
And it shows where the link really goes.

title.text: That's UniQR. One keypress, any QR code on your screen.

call.text: Each one gets a number. Press one. Done.

ticket.text: On my Mac, my ticket's one of those long barcodes.
Command, Shift, 8. It reads seven kinds of code, not just QR.

trap.text: Look closer. That link really goes somewhere else.

more.text: Two screens? It scans both at once.
A page full of codes? Every one gets a number.
Dots, logos, dark mode. It still reads them.
And if Win+Shift+Q is already taken?
more.say: And if Win, Shift, Q is already taken?

more.text: On Windows, it moves to the next free one, and tells you. Or pick your own.
Does it start on its own?
At login, if you say yes. And your scans never leave your machine.

proof.text: 96.8% of 1,064 test codes decoded. Zero wrong answers.
proof.say: Ninety-six point eight percent of a thousand sixty-four test codes. Zero wrong answers.

proof.text: And the C++ version scans in a median of 5 milliseconds.
proof.say: And the C plus plus version scans in a median of five milliseconds.
